title: async staging bucket coalescer tuning and ghost allocation investigation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are seeing gradual growth of pinned host / staging memory and unexplained resident GPU footprints during continuous-batching KV cache warmups. This ticket captures an investigation into the async staging "coalescer" (the internal bucket merge/defrag path used before handing pages to cudaMallocAsync) and a class of 'ghost' allocations that remain resident across batch boundaries. The goal is to identify root cause(s), validate mitigations, and land a low-risk runtime change + telemetry so regressions are detectable.
steps_to_repro:
1) Run continuous-batching load generator (kv_warmup_sweep) with sequence length distribution matching chat-service-prod (p50=128, p95=512) on a single GPU node using current runtime image (runtime-1.19-canary).
2) Enable KV prefetching with kv_prefetch=on and staging_pool=async.
3) Instrument the run for 90 minutes. Observe host pinned and GPU resident metrics from metrics/runtime and node exporter.
4) Compare with a control run with kv_prefetch=off.
Expected: in problematic runs, pinned staging grows ~50-300MB/hour and sometimes plateaus at high water mark; control run remains stable.
observations:
- Growth pattern is linear while KV prefetch is active and continuous batching rate is high.
- Sampling of allocator stacks (malloc_trace) shows allocations attributed to the staging coalescer path and a handful of allocations with empty backtraces (likely async/free lag).
- cublas/cudnn activity does not correlate with the spikes; growth correlates tightly with prefetch window size and batch overlap.
- Canary with a conservative coalescer threshold (reduce merge batch size by 40%) reduced host-pinned growth by ~70% in one run.
- Fragmentation fingerprinting shows higher external fragmentation after long runs; free lists have many small leftover arenas unusable for new large KV slices.
hypothesis:
1) The staging coalescer is producing many small pinned staging allocations because its merge heuristics favor low-latency returns over large contiguous blocks; this increases fragmentation and prevents efficient cudaMallocAsync reuse.
2) There is delayed async-free sequencing on certain CUDA streams causing 'ghost' pages to remain resident beyond when the runtime thinks they are freed (in-flight frees held by other streams), amplified by KV prefetch concurrency.
3) The current slab/pool thresholds are not adapting to the changed allocation size distribution introduced by prefetch + continuous batching, resulting in repeated allocation/deallocation churn and allocator drift.
experiments: Experiment A: Lower coalescer merge threshold and increase max-merge-window to favor larger contiguous pinned blocks (canary runtime build: pr/ENG-83190/coalesce-tune). Result: host-pinned growth down ~70% in single-run smoke test.

Experiment B: Add per-stream free-epoch tagging and force stream-synchronization during staging free path for 10-minute window to validate in-flight-free hypothesis. Result: immediate drop in ghost-residency but increased tail latency; indicates correctness of hypothesis 2 but cost tradeoff is unacceptable for default path.

Experiment C: Adjust pool bucket sizes to bias toward medium-size buckets (>>64KB, <<8MB) and add eviction of long-unused small arenas after 5m idle. Result: fragmentation index improved, reuse rate up ~25%.
Experiment D: Add high-cardinality telemetry (alloc_backtrace_signature, staging_bucket_histogram, stream_free_epoch) to canary to collect richer signals over longer runs.
Experiment E: Run workload with cudaMemPoolSetAttribute heuristics toggled (when available) to prefer reuse vs immediate release; measured small improvements but not sufficient alone.
next_steps: 1) Run extended canary (48h) with PR-1487 + PR-1495 on a small fleet (3 nodes) under synthetic continuous-batching replicate of prod mix. Watch fragmentation index and pinned_growth rate. (owner: Kunal)
2) If canary stable, land coalescer tuning behind a runtime flag and create rollout plan with 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% steps, monitoring pinned_staging and tail latency. (owner: Release Eng)
3) Author a microbenchmark that reproduces allocation-size distribution observed in prod and add to CI gating to prevent regressions. (owner: Performance Eng)
4) Follow-up: explore lightweight stream-quarantine for frees that are suspected to be in-flight, but keep it opt-in due to latency cost. (owner: Infra SRE)
